To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the available transfer capability is the maximum power flow between two points in a network that can be transferred without violating any operational constraints.
the available transfer capability is a function of the state of the system, the forecasted state of the system and the risk of congestion.

ATC can be determined by using a linear programming model that includes the effects of congestion management and uncertainty on the state of the system, and that the resulting ATC is more accurate than that determined by existing methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the assessment of available transfer capability (including the congestion cost), the risk of curtailed power, and the impact on the security of the power system of the use of the available transfer capability; the development of a methodology to determine available transfer capability and the congestion cost associated with it; and the development of a method to assess the impact on the power system of a use of the available transmission capacity.
the development of an approach for determining the available transfer capability (atc) between two zones.
the assessment of the congestion cost associated with the available transfer capability and the risk of transmission curtailment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the available transfer capability is a measure of the transfer capability that is available to a transmitting entity for a specific transmission path between two specific points, under specific conditions, and for a specific period of time.
the available transfer capability is a very important concept that should be used with care, as its calculation is not a trivial task.
the ATC concept is an important step toward a more efficient and competitive electric power industry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new approach that provides the ATC by taking into account the congestion management.
we have proposed a new method for the assessment of the available transfer capability (atC) that takes into account the risk of curtailement.
we have developed a method to assess the risk of curtailed power and the cost of congestion in an open market.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the available transfer capability is not a constant but rather a random variable that depends on the state of the system.
the uncertainty of the system state forecast can lead to significant overestimation of ATC and to the underestimation of the congestion cost.
a realistic assessment of the congestion cost of a transfer is possible by using a probabilistic approach.
